seating capacity was sufficient for thirty-four persons besides the driver. Along each side, outside the car, was a platform nine inches wide, affording standing room for twenty persons. After the thirty-four passengers had taken their places other comers were admitted only on sufferance, and although they paid fare they had to seek their own comfort,—rather a forlorn hope,—the only solace being the consideration of a ride on a railroad;—a slight improvement on 'riding on a rail.' There was not an apology for a spring about the car to relieve the monotony of the incessant jar. Passengers complained of the tremor causing their heads to itch. The oldest physician now living in West Chester, after he had ridden a few miles out and returned, gave it as his opinion that the constant jarring might be productive of concussion of the brain. A joker within bearing remarked that 'if Dr. T's theory is correct we shall soon be a community of addle-pates.' The car was drawn by one horse, of which John Griffith (old Griffy as he was familiarly called), was the driver."

Of the cars used on the Philadelphia and Columbia on the day it was formally opened, in 1834, it is stated that "there were two trains, each consisting of thirty four-wheeled cars, each car seating sixteen persons, eight on a side." Some of these cars were constructed by stagecoach builders.

Of the cars which passed over the Portage Railroad about 1834, Mr. W. Milnor Roberts who had charge of its operation, says:—
"The freight cars were all four-wheeled, weighing from three to three and a half net tons each, or six thousand to seven thousand pounds. The passenger cars first used were of the primitive formation, designed and put upon the road by Mr. Lot Dixon, one of my assistant engineers. They seated comfortably twenty-five persons inside, and, like the interior of a modern street car, accommodated an indefinite number outside."

On the Philadelphia, Germantown and Norristown Railroad cars of the stage-coach pattern were at first used. Of later devices one of its early employees says that the company "adopted a new form of coach, more nearly approximating the modern pattern of a steam railroad car. These were constructed by joining two of the old carriages together, making an eight-wheeled car, with a door at each end; and a passage way through the middle."

Finding the Right Therapist: Key Considerations

Finding the right therapist is crucial for effective trauma recovery. It’s important to look for a licensed professional with specialized training in trauma therapy, as their expertise can make a significant difference in the therapeutic process. Consider factors such as the therapist’s experience, approach to treatment, and familiarity with different trauma modalities. Personal compatibility is also vital; a supportive and empathetic therapist can create a safe space for healing.

Don’t hesitate to ask potential therapists about their qualifications and treatment methods. Many therapists offer initial consultations, allowing you to gauge your comfort level and discuss your specific needs. Trust your instincts when choosing a therapist; you should feel heard, respected, and supported in your healing journey. Remember, finding the right therapist can take time, but this investment is essential for achieving lasting recovery from trauma.

Online Resources: Expanding Your Support Network

In today’s digital age, online resources have become invaluable for those seeking support in trauma recovery. Websites, forums, and apps can offer a wealth of information on trauma therapy, coping strategies, and self-care techniques. Many organizations provide online courses and webinars led by experienced professionals, making it easier for individuals to access quality information from the comfort of their homes.

Moreover, online communities can help individuals connect with others who share similar experiences, reducing feelings of isolation. Social media platforms and dedicated support groups offer spaces where people can share their journeys and support one another. These online resources are not a substitute for professional therapy but can complement traditional treatment by providing additional support, information, and a sense of community during the recovery process.

Support Groups: Connecting with Others Who Understand

Support groups can play a significant role in the recovery journey by providing a safe space for individuals to share their experiences with trauma. Connecting with others who have faced similar challenges fosters a sense of belonging and validation. In these groups, participants can exchange coping strategies, insights, and encouragement, creating a supportive environment for healing. This shared understanding helps alleviate feelings of isolation and encourages individuals to open up about their struggles.

Many support groups are facilitated by professionals trained in trauma recovery, ensuring that discussions remain constructive and focused on healing. Online and in-person options are available, allowing individuals to choose what feels most comfortable. Participating in a support group can empower individuals to confront their trauma, reinforce their recovery goals, and build meaningful connections with others on a similar journey.

These resources are designed by experts in supply chain management and will help familiarize you with the content and format of the exam.

Another valuable source of free CSCP Certification Study Material is online forums and communities dedicated to supply chain professionals. Here, you can find discussions about recommended books, articles, and even downloadable PDFs shared by individuals who have already successfully passed their CSCP exam.

Additionally, many educational institutions and training providers offer free webinars or recorded lectures covering key topics relevant to the CSCP certification. These sessions often include downloadable slides or handouts that can serve as excellent study aids.

It’s important to note that while these free downloads are incredibly helpful in supplementing your preparation efforts, they should not be solely relied upon. It’s still advisable to invest in comprehensive CSCP Certification Study Material such as textbooks or online courses specifically designed for CSCP certification.

Taking advantage of free downloads available for CSCP Certification Study Material can greatly enhance your preparation process without straining your budget. So why not take advantage of them? Remember though – use them wisely alongside other reputable sources to ensure a well-rounded approach towards acing your CSCP certification!

How to Utilize the CSCP Certification Study Material Effectively

Effective utilization of CSCP Certification Study Material is crucial for success in any certification exam, including the CSCP. Here are some tips on how to make the most out of your CSCP study materials.

It’s important to create a study schedule and stick to it. Break down your study material into manageable chunks and allocate specific times for each topic or module. This will help you stay organized and ensure that you cover all the necessary content before your exam.

When studying, try to actively engage with the material rather than passively reading through it. Take notes, highlight key points, and ask yourself questions as you go along. This will help reinforce your understanding of the concepts and improve retention.

Additionally, supplementing your study materials with Additional Resources can be beneficial. Look for online forums or discussion boards where you can interact with other CSCP candidates or industry professionals. These platforms often provide valuable insights and real-world examples that can enhance your learning experience.

The Internationalization Core Working Group (principals and alternates) will communicate using a variety of mailing lists. These include:

Group Participation

Each participating W3C Member organization participates with one main representative. A W3C Member organization can designate one or more alternates for additional work. An alternate can serve as a fallback when the main representative is temporarily unavailable. The chair can accept additional alternates to allow a W3C Member organization to provide more resources to the Working Group.

All Working Group participants should be prepared to spend up to 20% of their working time on the WG. If a W3C Member organization designates one or more alternates, the 20% is to be understood as the total time devoted to the WG by the main representative and alternates, excluding the time needed by them for internal coordination. For more details about participation requirements, please see the Process Document.

Members of the Working Group must produce deliverables as agreed by the WG, and attend face-to-face meetings and regular (generally weekly) teleconferences. Between meetings and teleconferences, the Working Group maintains several mailing lists for appropriate discussion.

The initial Chair of this Working Group is Addison Phillips (webMethods, Inc.).

W3C Team Contact

The initial W3C Team contact is Martin Dürst. It is expected that this Group will consume about 0.5 FTE, including administrative logistics.

Patent Policy

This Working Group operates under the W3C Patent Policy (5 February 2004 Version). To promote the widest adoption of Web standards, W3C seeks to issue Recommendations that can be implemented, according to these policies, on a Royalty-Free basis.

For information about patent disclosures or exclusions regarding specifications produced by this Working Group, please refer to the Working Group home page.

Work onCharacter Model for the World Wide Web 1.0: Fundamentals and Character Model for the World Wide Web 1.0: Resource Identifiers is carried out under the 24 January 2002 CPP as amended by the W3C Patent Policy Transition Procedure.

Addison Phillips (webMethods, Inc.), Chair, W3C I18N WG

Information & Guides

Learning the Art of Body Piercing

Learning the art of body piercing from the comfort of one's home is an accessible and viable option for aspiring piercers. While hands-on apprenticeships in professional studios remain the gold standard for comprehensive training, there are several avenues for individuals to begin their journey into body piercing from home.

1. Online Courses and Tutorials

Many experienced piercers and reputable organizations offer online courses and tutorials covering essential topics, such as anatomy, sterilization techniques, piercing procedures, and aftercare. These digital resources provide a structured curriculum and valuable insights, enabling learners to acquire foundational knowledge at their own pace.

2. Books and Literature

A wealth of literature on body piercing is available in the form of books, e-books, and academic papers. Aspiring piercers can delve into these resources to gain insights into the history of piercing, modern techniques, and jewelry selection.

3. Virtual Workshops and Webinars

Participating in virtual workshops and webinars led by experienced piercers offers interactive learning opportunities. These live sessions allow learners to ask questions, receive feedback, and engage in discussions with industry professionals.

4. Online Communities and Forums

Joining online forums and social media groups dedicated to body piercing provides a platform for learning from experienced practitioners. Engaging with the community fosters networking opportunities, access to valuable insights, and sharing of experiences.

5. Practice Kits and Models

To gain practical experience, individuals can invest in body piercing practice kits, which include simulation skin and needles designed for safe practice. These kits allow learners to practice techniques and develop dexterity under controlled conditions.

6. Mentorship and Consultations

Seeking mentorship from experienced piercers for guidance and constructive feedback can be valuable. Connecting with established professionals through virtual consultations can offer personalized advice and direction for improvement.

7. Compliance with Local Regulations

While learning from home, it is crucial to understand and comply with local regulations and licensing requirements for body piercing. Familiarizing oneself with health and safety guidelines ensures responsible learning practices.

8. Ongoing Learning and Certification

As learners progress in their journey, pursuing certifications from recognized piercing organizations and attending industry seminars and conferences can enhance their credibility and skillset.
